title: Brain
summary: The brain is the control center of the body - a soft, wrinkled organ that thinks, feels, moves, and remembers. Explore its main regions and how each one handles a different kind of job.

compareCandidate.label: Brain vs. computer
compareCandidate.description: The brain is sometimes compared to a computer, but it is different: it is soft tissue made of living cells, it learns and changes with experience, and it runs the whole body's automatic functions while also thinking and feeling.

plainLanguageExplanation: The brain is the body's control center, made of billions of neurons (nerve cells) packed together. It has several main regions. The cerebrum, the big wrinkled outer part, handles thinking, sensing, and voluntary movement; its two halves are the right and left hemispheres, and its lobes do different jobs. The cerebellum at the back coordinates balance and smooth movement. The brainstem connects the brain to the spinal cord and runs automatic life jobs like breathing and heartbeat. Deep inside, the hippocampus helps form memories and the amygdala helps with emotions. The brain floats in fluid that cushions it, and is protected by the skull.

whyItMatters: The brain runs everything you do - every thought, memory, movement, and heartbeat. Understanding its main regions explains why a bump on the head or damage to one part affects specific skills, and how the brain coordinates the whole body.
didYouKnow: Your brain has about 86 billion neurons, and signals can travel between them at more than 100 meters per second.
